#!/bin/bash
# Restart a service on the deploy host and announce the release.

set -e

SERVICE=$1
VERSION=$2

REMOTE_HOST=deploy@deploy.example.internal
SLACK_URL=$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL

. etc/services.conf

# Per-service override, for example CONFIG_web=/etc/web/deploy.conf
eval "CONFIG=\$CONFIG_$SERVICE"

echo "deploying $SERVICE $VERSION with $CONFIG"

ssh $REMOTE_HOST "sudo systemctl restart $SERVICE && /usr/local/bin/deploy $SERVICE $VERSION"

curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"text\": \"Deployed $SERVICE $VERSION by $USER\"}" $SLACK_URL
# deploy-tools

Deployment helpers for the internal services.

`bin/notify-deploy.sh SERVICE VERSION` restarts the service on the deploy host and posts a
message to the release channel. The webhook URL comes from `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` in the
environment; per-service settings live in `etc/services.conf`.
.

cat > bin/notify-deploy.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Restart a service on the deploy host and announce the release.
#
# Usage: notify-deploy.sh [--dry-run] SERVICE VERSION [NOTE]

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 [--dry-run] SERVICE VERSION [NOTE]" >&2
  exit 2
}

DRY_RUN=0
ARGS=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case $arg in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    *) ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done
set -- "${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}"

[ $# -ge 2 ] && [ $# -le 3 ] || usage

SERVICE=$1
VERSION=$2
NOTE=${3-}

# These two are interpolated into a remote shell command, so restrict them.
[[ $SERVICE =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || { echo "invalid service name" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $VERSION =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+$ ]] || { echo "invalid version" >&2; exit 2; }

REMOTE_HOST=deploy@deploy.example.internal
SLACK_URL=${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL-}

# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. etc/services.conf

# Per-service override, for example CONFIG_web=/etc/web/deploy.conf
CONFIG_VAR="CONFIG_${SERVICE//[.-]/_}"
CONFIG=${!CONFIG_VAR-}

MESSAGE="Deployed $SERVICE $VERSION by ${USER:-unknown}"
if [ -n "$NOTE" ]; then
  MESSAGE+=$'\n'"Release note: $NOTE"
fi

REMOTE_CMD="sudo systemctl restart $SERVICE && /usr/local/bin/deploy $SERVICE $VERSION"
PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --arg text "$MESSAGE" '{text: $text}')

echo "deploying $SERVICE $VERSION with ${CONFIG:-<no config>}"

if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "[dry-run] would run on $REMOTE_HOST: $REMOTE_CMD"
  echo "[dry-run] would POST to Slack webhook (${SLACK_URL:+set}${SLACK_URL:-NOT SET}): $PAYLOAD"
  exit 0
fi

[ -n "$SLACK_URL" ] || { echo "SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is not set" >&2; exit 1; }

ssh "$REMOTE_HOST" "$REMOTE_CMD"

curl -sS --fail -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' -d "$PAYLOAD" "$SLACK_URL"
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Options

    bin/notify-deploy.sh [--dry-run] SERVICE VERSION [NOTE]

- `NOTE` (optional third argument): a short release note, appended to the Slack message as
  `Release note: ...`. Quote it so the shell passes it as one argument, e.g.
  `bin/notify-deploy.sh web 1.4.2 "Fixes login timeout"`. It is JSON-encoded, so quotes and
  special characters are safe.
- `--dry-run`: print what would happen (the remote command and the Slack payload) without
  restarting the service or posting the message. The flag may appear anywhere in the arguments.

`SERVICE` and `VERSION` may only contain letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` (and `+` in the version).
EOF
shellcheck bin/notify-deploy.sh; SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=x bash bin/notify-deploy.sh web 1.2 'say "hi" $(id)' --dry-run

content.text:
`bin/notify-deploy.sh` now takes an optional release note as a third argument and a `--dry-run` flag, and the README documents both. I only ran it with `--dry-run`, so the real ssh restart and Slack post are untested.

I ran a dry run with a note containing quotes and `$(id)`. The payload came out as plain text, and nothing was executed. `shellcheck` reports only an info-level note (SC2029) about `$REMOTE_CMD` expanding on the client side, which is intended here.

- **Release note:** `bin/notify-deploy.sh web 1.4.2 "Fixes login timeout"` adds a `Release note: …` line to the Slack message. I build the payload with `jq`, so quotes and special characters in the note can't break the JSON.
- **`--dry-run`:** it prints the remote command and the Slack payload, and says whether the webhook URL is set without printing it. It doesn't run ssh or curl. The flag works in any position.
- **README:** it has a new "Options" section covering both.

I also changed some existing behaviour, because I was editing those lines anyway:
- **Input checks:** `SERVICE` and `VERSION` are checked against a safe character set, because they go into the remote shell command. Anything with other characters is now rejected.
- **No more `eval`:** the per-service `CONFIG_<service>` lookup uses indirect expansion instead.
- **Quoting and errors:** variables are quoted, and the script uses `set -euo pipefail`. It prints usage and exits 2 if the arguments are wrong, and curl now fails on an HTTP error. A real run also errors out if `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is unset, before anything is restarted.
- **`jq` dependency:** the script now needs `jq` installed. It is present on this machine.
